findings.title: 4 indexable pages have no canonical tag
findings.why: With no canonicals anywhere, search engines choose among the slash, parameter and tracking variants of every page themselves.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing absolute canonical to every indexable page through the shared metadata helper.

findings.title: 4 indexable pages have no title, or all share one default title
findings.why: The title is the headline in search results. With none, or one default title such as “Create Next App” on almost every page, search engines write their own and every page looks the same.
findings.fix: Give every page a unique title through the shared metadata helper.

findings.title: 4 indexable pages have no H1
findings.why: Almost no page states its topic in a main heading, so search engines have to guess what each page is about.
findings.fix: Give every page template one H1 that names the page's topic.

findings.title: 6 pair(s) of indexable pages share most of their main content
findings.why: Pages that differ only by a swapped name (a city, product or tool) look like doorway or scaled content. Google can filter them out or hold down the whole site.
findings.fix: Give each page its own substance: specific details, local proof, its own intro and FAQs. Merge or noindex pages that can't be made unique.

findings.title: 4 description(s) are shared by more than one page
findings.what: 4 cases, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (Generated by create next app).
findings.why: Duplicate descriptions signal templated pages.
findings.fix: Write a specific description for each page.

findings.title: 3 page(s) below the home page have no BreadcrumbList
findings.why: Breadcrumb rich results still show in Google and clarify site structure.
findings.fix: Render BreadcrumbList from the same array as the visible breadcrumb.

findings.title: The home page has no Organization (or business) schema
findings.why: Organization schema identifies who runs the site and anchors every other schema node.
findings.fix: Add one Organization (or the right LocalBusiness subtype) node in the root layout with a stable `@id`.

findings.title: The site has no favicon that loads
findings.what: Found on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (no icon link on the home page, and /favicon.ico → 404).
findings.why: Google shows the site's favicon next to its name in search results. Without one that loads, results show a generic globe icon, which looks unfinished next to other sites' logos.
findings.fix: Add `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.png">` to the home page's `<head>`, pointing at a square PNG or ICO of at least 48 × 48 px that returns 200. Keep its URL stable and don't block it in robots.txt.

evidence.detail: no icon link on the home page, and /favicon.ico → 404

findings.title: The site is missing 5 recommended security header(s)
findings.why: Security headers protect visitors and are a trust signal, especially for technical audiences.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers at the server or framework level.

findings.title: 4 description(s) are outside 120–160 characters
findings.why: Short descriptions undersell the page; long ones get cut off.
findings.fix: Aim for 120–160 characters.

findings.title: 4 page(s) lack og:title or og:image
findings.why: Without og:title and og:image, shared links on Slack, LinkedIn and X show a bare URL instead of a card. Where og:description is listed too, the page has no description at all, so each platform guesses its text from the page or shows none.
findings.fix: Emit Open Graph and Twitter tags from the metadata helper, with a default image and per-page images for key pages, and og:description from the page's meta description.

findings.title: 4 indexable page(s) have fewer than 150 words
findings.why: A short page is worth a look, not a problem in itself: Google says there's no word count target, minimum or maximum. 150 words is our own line for a second look. A contact page or a calculator can do its job in few words.
findings.fix: If the page does its job, close this finding. If it doesn't, add useful, specific content, merge it into a stronger page, or noindex it until it grows.

findings.title: 4 indexable page(s) don't allow large image previews
findings.why: Without `max-image-preview:large`, Google shows small thumbnails at most, and pages are less likely to appear with large images in Discover.
findings.fix: Add `max-image-preview:large` to the robots meta of indexable pages through the metadata helper.

findings.title: 4 indexable page(s) have no structured data
findings.why: Schema tells search and AI engines what each page is.
findings.fix: Add the schema type the profile assigns to each page type.

findings.title: robots.txt doesn't reference the sitemap
findings.why: The `Sitemap:` line lets every crawler find it without manual submission.
findings.fix: Add `Sitemap: https://…/sitemap.xml` (absolute URL) to robots.txt.

findings.title: The site has no llms.txt
findings.why: llms.txt is a short Markdown map of a site's key pages, served at /llms.txt. Some AI tools and coding assistants read it to find their way around a site, which matters most for developer docs and API sites. SEO Supervisor asks for one because it makes the site easier for AI tools to read. It isn't a ranking factor: Google says an llms.txt file “will neither harm nor help your site's visibility or rankings in Google Search”, and no search engine says it ranks pages by it.
findings.fix: Serve a plain-text file at /llms.txt: a `# Site name` heading, a one-line `>` summary, then Markdown links to the key pages (`- [Page](https://…): one sentence`). A copy-ready example is in `examples/snippets.md`. Build it from the same data as the sitemap so it stays current. A site that doesn't want one can turn this check off in `seo-audit/settings.json`: `"checks": { "off": ["llms-txt-missing"] }`.

findings.title: No /.well-known/security.txt
findings.why: security.txt tells researchers how to report vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Publish one following RFC 9116 with Contact and Expires.

findings.title: The home page has no WebSite schema
findings.why: WebSite schema names the site and links pages to the organization.
findings.fix: Add a WebSite node with a stable `@id` and `publisher` pointing at the organization.

findings.title: No page asks the browser to start loading the next page early (speculation rules)
findings.why: Speculation rules let Chrome and Edge start loading a page as soon as a visitor shows they're about to open it (hovering over or pressing a link), so it appears almost at once. A few lines in the shared layout turn this on for the whole site; other browsers ignore them.
findings.fix: Add `<script type="speculationrules">{"prefetch":[{"where":{"href_matches":"/*"},"eagerness":"moderate"}]}</script>` to the shared layout, or send a `Speculation-Rules` header from the server or CDN. Leave out links that change something (log out, add to cart) with a `not` condition.

findings.title: No XML sitemap found (a small, well-linked site, so it matters less)
findings.why: Google says a site of about 500 pages or fewer, linked well enough that every important page can be found from the home page, and without many videos or news pages, might not need a sitemap. This crawl found every page through links from the home page, none more than three clicks deep. A sitemap still tells search engines when pages change, and lists a new page before any link to it exists.
findings.fix: Generate `/sitemap.xml` from the live content data and reference it in robots.txt, or leave it until the site grows.

trustSignals.label: About page
trustSignals.add: Add an About page that says who runs the site and why visitors can trust it, and link it from the main menu or the footer.

trustSignals.label: Contact details
trustSignals.add: Add a Contact page, or show an email address or phone number, and link it from every page.

trustSignals.label: Organization schema
trustSignals.add: Add Organization schema (or your business type) to the home page with the business's `name`, `logo` and `sameAs` links to its official profiles.

trustSignals.label: Author names
trustSignals.add: Name the author on each article, on the page and as `author` in its Article schema.

trustSignals.label: Author pages
trustSignals.add: Link each author's name to a page about them (role, experience, credentials), and give the author a `url` in the schema.

trustSignals.label: Dates on articles
trustSignals.add: Show when each article was published or last reviewed, and add `datePublished` and `dateModified` to its schema. Change them only with real edits (CONTENT-12).

trustSignals.label: Sources cited
trustSignals.add: Link the source next to each fact and figure in your content.

trustSignals.label: Customer reviews
trustSignals.add: Show real reviews, testimonials or case studies from customers. Only real ones count: never invent or edit them.

trustSignals.label: Policies
trustSignals.evidence: no link to a privacy policy
trustSignals.add: Add a privacy policy and link it from the footer.

trustSignals.label: HTTPS and security headers
trustSignals.evidence: https://zero.example; its missing security headers were read from a local build, which may lack the ones production adds
trustSignals.add: Serve every page over HTTPS and fix the open security findings (TRUST-01, TRUST-07).

trustSignals.label: Own images
trustSignals.add: Use your own photos, screenshots or diagrams on content pages, rather than none or stock photos.
